hook_text: One equation. Infinitely many answers. And you can write ALL of them in a single line.
clip_script: Here's an equation with infinitely many answers: sine x equals a half. Sounds impossible to finish, right? Watch. A taxi runs a loop through town, and you spot it passing your gate at seven. The loop takes an hour. So when else does it pass? Eight. Nine. Ten. And it passed at six, and at five. One sighting plus the loop time gives you the whole timetable: seven, plus k hours, for any whole number k — forwards or backwards. Trig equations work exactly like that. The wheel repeats every three hundred and sixty degrees — that's the loop. The calculator gives you one sighting: thirty degrees. But sine hits a half twice per loop — once on the way up, once on the way down — so there's a second door at one eighty minus thirty: one fifty. Now write the timetable: thirty plus k three sixty, or one fifty plus k three sixty. That single line holds every answer that ever existed. Need the ones between minus three sixty and three sixty? Run k through the small numbers and keep what lands inside: minus three thirty, minus two ten, thirty, one fifty. Four answers, netted from infinity, in four lines.
visual_style: A minibus taxi circling a looped route on a hand-drawn township map, clock faces stamping each pass; the route morphing into a spinning wheel with two glowing doors at 30 and 150 degrees; a timetable writing itself line by line.
mood: Playful, streetwise, the pleasure of taming something infinite.
pacing: Bold claim up front, relaxed through the taxi story, crisp and rhythmic through the harvest.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to write infinity in one line.
